qAndA.question: What was once considered impossible in astronomy?

qAndA.question: Why was it so difficult to capture an image of a black hole?

qAndA.answer: They created a virtual Earth-sized telescope by linking eight telescopes around the world.
qAndA.question: How did scientists overcome the challenge of observing the black hole?

text_to_speech: Astronomers Capture First Image of a Black Hole Astronomers have captured the shadow of a supermassive black hole... ...revealing a dark shadow set against a glowing disc of superheated gas and dust. This feat was once considered impossible... ...as black holes cast only small, difficult-to-observe shadows. Scientists linked up eight telescopes across the globe... ...facing extreme conditions at isolated locations... ...to create the Earth-sized Event Horizon Telescope. This unprecedented result heralds a new age of black hole exploration, paving the way for further breakthroughs. Transcribed by ESO; translated by –

youtube_description:
The Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) -- a planet-scale array of eight ground-based radio telescopes forged through international collaboration -- was designed to capture images of a black hole. In coordinated press conferences across the globe, EHT researchers revealed that they succeeded, unveiling the first direct visual evidence of a supermassive black hole and its shadow.

The video is available in 4K UHD.

The ESOcast Light is a series of short videos bringing you the wonders of the Universe in bite-sized pieces. The ESOcast Light episodes will not be replacing the standard, longer ESOcasts, but complement them with current astronomy news and images in ESO press releases.

More information and download options: http://www.eso.org/public/videos/eso1907b/
